newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-NRG EYES ESTONIA POWER EXPORTS.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-NRG EYES ESTONIA POWER EXPORTS.

text.p: NRG Energy a subsidiary of Northern States Power , is looking to Estonia to provide a base for exporting power to the Baltic region, NRG's representative in Estonia, Hillar Lauri, said on Tuesday.
"When we look at the future we see energy demand growing in neighbouring countries," he told Reuters in an interview.
"In our long-term planning we are also considering exporting power northwards, eastwards and southwards," Lauri said.
Estonia already exports electricity to Latvia, Russia and Lithuania. Exports in 1996 were up by 9.5 percent compared to 1995 with exports to Russia resuming, according to Estonian Energy figures.

NRG, the Estonian government and Estonian Energy are preparing a business plan for a possible 50/50 deal which would give the international power provider a foothold in Europe. However, the plan is far from complete.
"An agreement was signed on December 9 to go into business together and the joint business plan must be ready by July 1," Lauri said.
NRG is looking at investments worth over $250 million.
"The project involves a lot of money. About $50 million in NRG equity and $200 million in project finance," said Lauri.
NRG, which operates power plants in Australia and the United States, is looking forward to cooperation, there is no gaurantees they will be the main business partner for Estonian Energy.
But the Estonian government appears keen on selling off its power production.
"We have three months to go, if the plan does not suit the Americans, then there are others," Estonian Finance Minister Mart Opmann told Reuters in a recent interview.
The Estonian proposals are based on avoiding giving fixed prices and guaranteeing market share.
However, even if an agreement business plan is reached there is a crucual hurdle to be passed--the new energy bill which is before parliament.
This law regulating energy in Estonia has yet to define what can and cannot be sold off in Estonia's privisation drive from production to tranmission to distribution.
"NRG is interested in just the production with the debate on what should stay in state hands focused on tranmission," Lauri said.
